summary: The change gives every stop a run marker and resumes at the label the error names. Earlier prompts stay byte-identical and replay from cache, and the loop and prefs tests pin it closely. The findings are mostly where `run check` and the relaunch disagree: some folders a run wrote are missing from the marker (a stopped run, a post error after round 1), and some hand commits are never excused (after a non-error stop, or on a second resume at the same label). Smaller ones: a stale marker after a non-resumable error, a settings question asked before the resume choice, and a resume line that promises duplicate checks two Finish operations lack. The guard did not let the reviewer run node or shell scripts, so every finding comes from reading the code, not from running it.

findings.title: run check refuses the run's own files when the result does not list their folder
findings.description:
`run save` builds `specFolders` only from the result's `specFolders` and `snapshotStart` (lines 158-161). `run check`'s untracked rule (line 210) then treats any path outside those folders as stray. This breaks two cases.

(1) A record with no result (kind `stopped`) gets `specFolders: []`, and the prefs test pins that value. Such a run always has untracked files of its own. The skill writes `snapshot-start.json` before launch, and it stays untracked until a commit holds it (this round's own `agent-os/specs/2026-11-01-0935-59-review-round-1/redline/snapshot-start.json` is untracked right now). Each round also leaves review and reply files. So every `stopped` resume is refused with "commit or remove <the run's own files>, or start fresh". Removing `snapshot-start.json` would break the baseline checker.

(2) An error at `post r<n>` in any round after the first. The post agent writes `round-<n>-review.json` and `round-<n>-findings.json` before posting (postPrompt step 1). The round joins `rounds`, and so `result.specFolders`, only after `post()` returns (redline-loop.js 2864-2866). A GitHub failure at `post r2` is therefore refused as untracked. Committing those files, as the line suggests, turns the refusal into `head-moved`.

findings.title: A .claude/ hand commit passes the check for every kind but is excused only on an error resume
findings.description:
`run check` accepts commits on top of the marker's head that touch only `.claude/`, whatever the marker's `kind` (lines 192-207). Only the `error` resume carries them into the workflow, as `args.resume[label].hand` (SKILL.md line 76).

For `handoff`, `reviewed` and `stopped`, the skill relaunches with the marker's args plus decisions or selected, or unchanged (SKILL.md 77-78). `handCommits` and `handPaths` are then empty. The next `check r<n>` reports the hand commit as `commits without the redline: prefix` and its path as `files outside the approved plan changed`. The repair cannot undo a commit, so the run ends in error at `recheck`. The error resume that follows computes `hand` from the new marker's head, which is already past that commit, so the commit is never excused.

Example: a run stops at a hand-off, the person commits a `.claude/settings.json` permission fix, and Resume passes `run check`. The relaunch then fails at check r1 on that commit. The loop test's "an unexcused unexpected file still fails" pins the workflow side of this.
findings.proposedFix:
Decision needed: should a `.claude/` hand commit after a hand-off, a review-dial stop or a stopped run be refused, or carried?
- Refuse it: in `run check`, refuse a moved HEAD unless `marker.kind` is `error` (the README's reason for the `.claude/` rule is a gate fix after an error). Add a prefs-test case for a handoff marker with a `.claude/` commit on top, and adjust the README Launching sentence.
- Carry it: pass `hand` into the workflow for every kind, through an args field the judge reads. This changes what the workflow reads and is larger.

findings.title: Settings are asked and saved before the resume question
findings.description:
Section 3 (settle the settings: ask, then `redline-prefs.sh save`) runs before section 4. Whether the launch is a resume is only decided by the new "A stopped run" step at the top of section 4.

Read in order, the skill asks the settings question and saves the answers, then asks "Resume it, or start fresh?". On Resume those answers are thrown away, since args come from the marker. The clause on this line, "skip this ... on a resume (section 4, \"A stopped run\")", cannot be followed, because the resume choice has not been made yet. The Resume bullet's "skip sections 3, 4 and 5" comes after section 3 has already run.

Words typed on the command line (`dry run`, `no push`, `autopilot`) are also dropped on a resume without a word.
findings.proposedFix: Move "A stopped run" to a step between sections 2 and 3, right after the PR number is parsed, so a Resume skips sections 3 to 5 before anything is asked. On Resume, say in one line that the run resumes with its original settings, and name any typed word that was ignored.

findings.title: A second resume at the same label drops the first resume's hand commits
findings.description:
The error resume writes `{attempt, error, hand: <the check's hand>}` under the marker's label, replacing any entry already there. `run check` computes `hand` only from the marker's head to HEAD (redline-prefs.sh 196-198).

When the same label fails again after a resume (a gate fix that was not enough), the new marker's head already holds the first hand commit, so the new entry names only the second. The workflow's `handCommits` and `handPaths` lose the first. The rerun `recheck r1` then reports it as `commits without the redline: prefix` and its path as outside the approved plan, and every later attempt fails the same way.

Trace:
1. Error at `recheck r1`; hand commit H1 on `.claude/redline/checks.json`.
2. Resume, attempt 2; it still fails, giving resumeFrom `{recheck r1, 3}` and a marker whose head is H1.
3. Hand commit H2 on `.claude/redline/checks.sh`.
4. The resume entry becomes `{attempt 3, hand {H2}}`.
5. `judge()`: `unexpected_files` still holds `.claude/redline/checks.json` (snapshot r1 is cached without it), and H1 is unprefixed.
findings.proposedFix:
Union the hand lists. When the label already has an entry in the marker's `args.resume`, the new entry's `hand.commits` and `hand.paths` are the old entry's plus the check's.

Do this in the script rather than the skill: have `run check` print `hand` already merged with `marker.args.resume[marker.label].hand`, so the skill copies one value.

Tests:
- prefs-test: a marker whose args carry a resume entry for its label, plus a new `.claude/` commit on top; `hand` lists both.
- loop-test: a resume carrying both commits passes the judge.

findings.title: A non-resumable error leaves the earlier stop's marker in place
findings.description:
When `resumeFrom` is null, the error handler writes no marker, and it also does not clear the marker an earlier stop of the same run left. `run save` would refuse and keep the old entry anyway; the prefs test "a refused save leaves the entry" pins that.

Example: a run stops at a hand-off (marker written). It is relaunched in the same session and then ends in a non-resumable error, such as `gather r2` finding the PR closed. The hand-off marker stays. The next `/redline:redline <n>` asks "stopped at a hand-off with k judgment calls open. Resume it?" If the check passes, the skill reads `result` from the marker's record file, which the relaunch (same run id) has overwritten with the error result.
findings.proposedFix: In the `resumeFrom` null branch, run `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/redline-prefs.sh run clear <repoRoot> <n>` before naming the folders, as the `done`, `capped` and `review-only` handlers do.

findings.title: The resume line promises duplicate checks two Finish operations lack
findings.description:
The resume line tells the rerun agent "What an earlier attempt already made stands (...), and the duplicate checks in your instructions apply". Two Finish operations a resume can land on have no duplicate check.

`handoff comment`: `finishPrompt` posts the comment (step 2) and then requests the review (step 3). When step 3 fails (a reviewer GitHub refuses), the agent reports an error and the stop names `handoff comment`. The resume reruns step 2 and posts a second `Redline handoff` comment, once per attempt.

`record commit`: when the push in step 3 is rejected, the commit already exists. The resume replays `record files` from cache with the same file list and reruns the commit. It fails with "nothing to commit" (the error the loop test's "record: the commit fails" scripts), so the resume never gets past it.
findings.proposedFix:
Give each operation a resume path in its prompt:
- `finishPrompt`: before step 2, check `redline-gh.sh pr-comments <pr>` for a comment whose body equals the written file, and skip the post when one exists.
- `recordCommitPrompt`: skip the commit when HEAD's subject is the record message and it holds the listed files, then push.

Alternatively, limit the resume line's duplicate-check sentence to the operations that have one. Either way, pin each with a loop-test resume at that label.
